cross_package_notes.note: Verified read-only cross-package alignment for /api/v1/local-browser/{extension,extension/authorize,internal} (self-authenticated device/node gateway endpoints using validExtensionOrigin, Bearer pairing/renewal SHA-256 digests, and cluster HMAC-SHA256) and /api/v1/me/browser* (under authenticated v1 with APIKeyRouteGate default-deny).

invariants_checked: Production defaults in config/config.yaml fail closed: enable_rbac defaults to enforced, enable_cross_tenant_access defaults to false, Langfuse tracing is absent/disabled unless explicitly configured, and SSRF/sandbox network defaults remain fail-closed.
Model catalog YAML/JSON definitions (model_catalog.yaml and provider catalogs) contain no embedded live credentials, internal host paths, or legacy weknora/wk_ identifiers.
Prompt templates and evaluation datasets under config/prompts/ contain no unsafe template execution directives or brand residues.

YAML loading, environment variable interpolation (${VAR:-default}), duration parsing, and ValidateConfig enforce valid registration modes, default tenant modes, OIDC URLs, and positive numeric bounds.

Security-critical boolean environment overrides (GENYEE_TENANT_ENABLE_RBAC, OIDC_AUTH_PKCE_ENABLED, OIDC_AUTH_ENABLE, DISABLE_REGISTRATION, GENYEE_TENANT_ENABLE_CROSS_TENANT_ACCESS, GENYEE_AUTH_COMPLEX_PASSWORD_ENABLED) parse via strconv.ParseBool so standard truthy '1' values work and malformed strings log a warning and preserve safe prior/default values instead of failing open.
GENYEE_* environment variable naming is consistent with zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: applyOIDCEnvOverrides and applyAuthAndTenantDefaults parsed OIDC_AUTH_PKCE_ENABLED, OIDC_AUTH_ENABLE, DISABLE_REGISTRATION, GENYEE_TENANT_ENABLE_RBAC, and GENYEE_TENANT_ENABLE_CROSS_TENANT_ACCESS with strings.EqualFold(value, 'true') instead of strconv.ParseBool, causing truthy '1' values or typos ('ture') to silently disable RBAC enforcement, OIDC PKCE, or invite-only registration.

invariants_checked: CustomFormatter sanitizes control characters (CR, LF, ESC, NUL, DEL) out of request_id and caller tokens across both default and custom GENYEE_LOG_FORMAT templates, preventing log-line forging and terminal escape injection.

LLM debug logging keeps directory permissions 0700 and file permissions 0600, confines request_id filenames inside llm_debug via strict identifier allowlisting, and synchronizes enabled/dir state under llmDebug.mu without data races.

Context cloning (CloneContext / CloneContextWithoutTrace) preserves Principal, TenantAPIKeyScope, SandboxTenantID, MemoryAllowedForAgent, BackgroundTask, and NonInteractiveOAuth markers, and ErrorWithFields clones caller-supplied logrus.Fields maps rather than mutating them in-place.

findings.summary: configureLLMDebugLog wrote llmDebug.dir/enabled without holding llmDebug.mu while LLMDebugEnabled/LLMDebugLog read llmDebug.enabled unlocked (triggering a data race under -race and failing to disable on LLM_DEBUG_LOG=false reconfigure); CustomFormatter.Format emitted unsanitized CR/LF/ESC bytes from request_id; and ErrorWithFields mutated caller-owned logrus.Fields maps in-place.

invariants_checked: JWT, InternalDispatch, X-API-Key (workspace and platform), EmbedAuth, and MCPEndpointAuth re-verify workspace membership/revocation, scope capabilities, origin/Sec-Fetch-Site CSRF guards, and inactive/disabled/suspended workspace status consistently while preserving tenant-optional identity escape routes and system-admin/platform-key inspection.
RBAC RequireRole and APIKeyRouteGate enforce viewer/contributor/editor/admin/owner/system_admin floors and default-deny undeclared routes for machine API keys.

Access logger bounds request body peeks to maxBodySize+1 without consuming downstream streams, skips secret/vault/credential route bodies entirely, redacts sensitive JSON/form/header/query fields (including presigned sig/signature, ticket, code, api_key, client_secret, password), and validates X-Request-ID against header/log injection.
Panic Recovery middleware logs full stack traces server-side while returning generic HTTP 500 messages without leaking panic strings, DSNs, or internal addresses to clients.

findings.summary: Recovery() serialized raw fmt.Sprintf('%v', err) from panics directly into external HTTP 500 JSON responses (leaking internal SQL/DSN/secret strings on panic) and read dead c.Get('RequestID') instead of types.RequestIDContextKey.

Unlike MCPEndpointAuth, JWT/InternalDispatch Auth, workspace API-key Auth, and EmbedAuth did not reject inactive/disabled/suspended workspaces (allowing continued API, embed, and workspace-key access to deactivated tenants), and attachAPIKeyAuthContext lacked a nil-tenant guard before dereferencing t.

sanitizeQuery omitted presigned URL HMAC parameters (sig, signature) and query secret keys (api_key, apikey, client_secret, secret, password) from access-log redaction, and RequestID() echoed arbitrary unvalidated X-Request-ID headers without length or visible-ASCII checks.

invariants_checked: Dead-letter middleware records terminal failures (SkipRetry or exhausted retries) while ignoring RevokeTask and transient retries, forwarding original handler errors unchanged.

Corrupt/non-UTF-8/malformed-JSON task payloads are safely base64-wrapped into valid UTF-8 JSON objects and invalid UTF-8 error strings are sanitized before rune-boundary truncation so PostgreSQL JSONB / MySQL JSON inserts never drop dead-letter rows.
RecoverMiddleware, CallRecovered, and safeInvokeCallback convert panics to errors without panicking on nil *asynq.Task pointers.

findings.summary: buildDeadLetter stored raw malformed/binary payloads directly in json.RawMessage and truncateError did not sanitize invalid UTF-8 bytes in short errors (causing json.Marshal and PostgreSQL JSONB / MySQL JSON inserts to fail and drop the dead-letter row); CallRecovered and safeInvokeCallback also dereferenced nil *asynq.Task on panic.

invariants_checked: Sliding-window per-minute Limiter and UTC per-day DailyLimiter enforce Redis Lua ZSET/INCR atomicity and fall back cleanly to bounded mutex-guarded in-memory counters when Redis is nil or unreachable.
Zero/negative maxPerMinute and maxPerDay values disable limiting as documented (unlimited), and background sweep loops bound in-memory map growth without data races under -race.

Every state-mutating and sensitive route across router.go and routes_*.go sits behind middleware.Auth (or dedicated EmbedAuth / MCPEndpointAuth / presigned HMAC / capability grant / BrowserSkill device-cluster auth), workspace RBAC guards (Viewer/Contributor/Editor/Admin/Owner/SystemAdmin), and APIKeyRouteGate policy assertions (assertAPIKeyPoliciesMatchRoutes + assertOperationRoutesExist).

trustedProxies defaults to loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1/128), skips malformed GENYEE_TRUSTED_PROXIES entries, and applyTrustedProxies fails closed to direct peer IP (SetTrustedProxies(nil)) if Gin rejects the list so X-Forwarded-For can never spoof ClientIP() for rate limiters.

buildCORSConfig disables AllowCredentials whenever wildcard '*' or empty allowlists apply, and rejects 'null' or non-http(s) malformed origins so sandboxed iframes cannot obtain credentialed CORS reflection and gin-contrib/cors never panics at startup.

File proxy surfaces (/files, KB files, message files, /api/v1/files/presigned, /api/v1/files/presigned-preview, /r/:token) enforce tenant path/resource ownership, constant-time HMAC signature verification, attachment Content-Disposition on active browser content, and redact internal storage backend errors.

findings.summary: r.SetTrustedProxies(trustedProxies()) logged errors without clearing Gin's default 0.0.0.0/0 trust list when GENYEE_TRUSTED_PROXIES contained any malformed IP/CIDR (failing open to X-Forwarded-For ClientIP spoofing across public rate limiters), and buildCORSConfig accepted 'null' and non-http(s) origins (risking credentialed null-origin CORS reflection or startup panics in cors.New).

servePresignedPreview discarded resolvedPath from resolveCatalogResource and passed raw 'resource://...' references to parseStorageTarget (failing every own-tenant resource preview with 400 'empty provider' and missing ResourceCatalogFileService wrapping when storageResolver was nil), and returned raw internal storage/signing err.Error() strings in HTTP JSON responses.

invariants_checked: AES-256-GCM encryption (crypto.go) enforces key derivation/length bounds, fresh cryptographic random nonces, and preserves the intentional negative security check rejecting legacy default 'weknora-system-aes-key*' secrets.
Presigned file URL signing (presign.go) enforces HMAC-SHA256 with hmac.Equal constant-time comparison, unix expiry validation, and canonical path/tenant binding.

SSRF and network validators (security.go, net_guard.go, url_validator.go) fail closed on loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, CGNAT, multicast, unspecified IPs, DNS rebinding via dial-time Control hooks, and cross-origin redirect hops.

Archive/path helpers and browser content-type guards (fileutil.go) block path traversal, active same-origin scripting extensions (including .svg/.html/.xhtml/.shtml/.mht/.mhtml/.xml/.xsl/.xslt/.rdf/.mathml/.js/.mjs/.css/.swf), directory-dot confusion, and trailing-dot/space extension bypasses.

findings.summary: IsActiveBrowserContentExt omitted active browser document/script formats (.shtml, .mht, .mhtml, .xsl, .xslt, .rdf, .mathml, .swf) and SafeContentTypeByFilename neither isolated the path basename nor stripped trailing dots/spaces (allowing 'payload.svg.' or 'payload.html ' to bypass inline Content-Disposition blocking).
